syllabus.clause: grounded in the Kafka design docs and the Raft paper. Durability vs availability is decided by which acknowledgement point is used: accepted by a subset, persisted by a quorum, or durably recorded by the leader. Kafka's acks, ISR and min.insync.replicas; Kafka has run KRaft-only (no ZooKeeper) since 4.0 (March 2025).

at.step: Measured: genuinely lost, once the leader that alone held the acknowledged write was destroyed
Measured: genuinely lost again, even though the write was durably recorded, because it never reached any node beyond the one that was destroyed
Measured: genuinely survives, on the identical leader destruction, because a real quorum already held a durable copy beyond just the leader

items.item: the leader will write the record to its local log but will respond without awaiting full acknowledgement from all followers; should the leader fail immediately after acknowledging the record but before the followers have replicated it then the record will be lost

at.step: Measured, in Kafka's own words: should the leader fail immediately after acknowledging the record but before the followers have replicated it, then the record will be lost

items.item: the leader will wait for the full set of in-sync replicas to acknowledge the record; this guarantees that the record will not be lost as long as at least one in-sync replica remains alive

items.item: All three policies run the identical write id through the identical cluster size and the identical leader-destruction function, so the measured difference in survival is attributable to the acknowledgement threshold alone, not to a different write, cluster, or failure.

items.item: The quorum size used here is computed from the real cluster size via a genuine majority function (num_nodes divided by two, plus one), not a hard-coded constant chosen to make the demonstration work, and it is checked against that independently computed expected value.

items.item: The surprising, stronger claim this topic measures is that durability on the leader alone genuinely fails identically to no durability at all, under node destruction, since neither write ever reached a second node; this is deliberately shown as its own separate step rather than folded into the subset case, so the distinction between 'durable' and 'replicated' stays visible.

at.step: Measured: genuinely lost again, even though the write was durably recorded, because it never reached any node beyond the one that was destroyed

items.item: Node destruction is modeled as the complete removal of that node's own state (not merely a process restart with its disk intact), matching Kafka's own documented guarantee of surviving as long as at least one in-sync replica remains alive, which implies the failure model it is built to tolerate is losing a node entirely.

items.item: All of this topic's own measured claims run entirely on plain in-memory Rust structs and vectors, with no real network I/O, root access, or real multiple machines needed; 'nodes' and 'destruction' are real, deterministic Rust values and function calls, continuing this domain's own established pattern of measuring a real, small, fully-controlled model directly.

items.item: The Kafka Producer Configuration Reference page and the Kafka Topic Configuration Reference page are two genuinely distinct documentation pages (one on how a producer requests an acknowledgement, the other on how a broker enforces a minimum replica count), giving this topic two independent primary sources rather than multiple quotes drawn from a single page.

items.item: The three-node cluster size used throughout this topic's own scenario is this specific example's own choice, matching the syllabus's own three-node lab exercise for this chapter; the measured claims illustrate the direction and shape of the real effect for any cluster size where a quorum is a genuine strict majority, not a claim bound to exactly three nodes.

items.item: The acknowledgement thresholds for the subset policy and the leader-only-durable policy are deliberately identical (both equal to one node), since the syllabus's own distinction between 'accepted by a subset' and 'durably recorded by the leader' is about durability semantics on that one node, not about how many nodes are involved; this topic's own measured result (both lose the write identically) is the real, intended answer to that distinction, not an oversight.
